source.title: Dialogue Injection Attack: Jailbreaking LLMs Through Context Manipulation
source.authors: Wen-Long Meng; Fan Zhang; W. Yao; Zhen-Yuan Guo; Yu-Wei Li; Cheng-Kun Wei; Wen-Zhi Chen

record.file_problem: none; the paper text includes the main sections and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: It adapts prefilling to a black-box dialogue-injection attack and reports harmful-jailbreak success rates, testing whether a prefixed affirmative opening can help bypass safety. It does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or token-wise KL measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper cites shallow safety alignment and prior prefilling work as motivation, but those cited results are not this study's results. Extracted DIA-I and DIA-II attack-success rates, plus the text-reported multi-query outcomes. The paper also reports other attacks, defenses, and ablations; they are not separate rows here because the selected rows capture the direct attack-performance results for the tested bypass claim.
record.test_reason: DIA-I adapts a prefilled affirmative opening to a black-box dialogue-injection setting and reports jailbreak success rates across models, so it bears on V4. The attacks are combined, so no row isolates prefilling. DIA-II does not prefill; it defers the answer through a word-substitution task.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is roughly right. The authors present DIA as a black-box jailbreak using injected dialogue history, effective against recent LLMs and able to bypass five defenses. They call for defenses that account for multi-turn context. They also say the prefilling vulnerability may have been partly patched in Llama-3.1.
record.recipe_differences: This study evaluates a black-box dialogue-injection jailbreak, including affirmative-prefix continuation and delayed-answer word substitution; it does not apply the original fine-tuning or token-wise KL measurement recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ASR varies across model families and sizes, benchmark, evaluator, attack method, and query iterations. The authors report LlamaGuard-3 generally gives higher ASRs than LlamaGuard-2.

fits_no_version.finding: DIA-II's deferral through a word-substitution task bypasses refusal (ASR 0.23 to 0.74 on AdvBench, LlamaGuard-2). The paper reports a higher log-likelihood for deferred harmful text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deferring the harmful answer behind benign text bypasses safety without a prefilled affirmative opening.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
record.problems: The reported rates depend on safety-classifier evaluators, and the paper notes that LlamaGuard-3 is stricter than LlamaGuard-2. The attacks combine multiple components, so the ASRs do not isolate the effect of prefilling alone. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted DIA-I LlamaGuard-3 results on HEx-PHI and MaliciousInstruct results (Tables 3 and 6), DIA-II results outside AdvBench/LlamaGuard-2 (Tables 2, 3, and 6), and the full iteration-by-model curves (Figures 5, 7, and 10). Also omitted the separate component-ablation and defense-pass-rate results (Tables 4 and 5), which do not isolate the prefilling effect.

untested.parts: No adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. Prefilling alone, without the system prompt replacement, hypnosis and guidance, is not tested. The ablation in Table 4 removes components but never removes the prefill.
No test of the cause of shallowness.

missing.what: Component ablation (system prompt, hypnosis, answer guidance removed) showing the DIA-I ASR on Llama-3-8B falls from 0.571 to 0.010 without the system prompt. This shows the prefill alone is insufficient on some models.
Log-likelihood of affirmative beginnings rises when benign text is prepended. This is a related finding about positional or contextual effects, not about first-token safety.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not a source for any version. Single-query rates have no baseline without the attack, and no uncertainty is reported. The Llama-3.1-8B DIA-I result of 0.000 (r04) is stated in the text as evidence that the prefill vulnerability may have been patched. The 'supports' label rests on combined-attack results, and the rows themselves note that prefilling is not isolated. The record's DIA-II rows (r31 to r40) should not carry 'supports' or 'limits_scope' for V4.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or resulting refusal/compliance rates are tested.
No fine-tuning on benign data or resulting harmful-compliance rates are tested.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
Tests a dialogue-injected affirmative beginning (DIA-I) and a word-substitution deferral attack (DIA-II); does not test adversarial suffixes or decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization is tested.
Does not test whether training data or objective causes safety to be shallow.
No training that spreads safety across response tokens or test of its robustness is conducted.

relationships.condition: DIA-I (prefill plus system prompt replacement, hypnosis and guidance) on Llama-3-8B, Gemma-2 9B/27B and Qwen-2-7B, AdvBench and HEx-PHI
relationships.reason: ASR is high (0.47 to 0.98). The attack is combined, so this supports a prefill-based bypass only in aggregate (r02, r06, r07, r08, r12, r16, r17, r18, r22, r26, r27, r28).
relationships.display_finding: ASR ranged from 0.47 to 0.98, but the attack combines prefill with other manipulations, so the prefill's own share is not isolated.

relation.reason: The study reports direct harmful-response rates for a composite prefill-based bypass, bearing on V4, although it does not isolate the affirmative prefix.

tranche.reason: DIA-I adapts affirmative-prefix continuation to black-box historical-dialogue injection and measures harmful-response success in this new setting.

source_check.notes: DIA-I measures a composite historical-dialogue attack; Gemma's replacement system instructions are incorporated into user text. Single-query limitations do not establish multi-query resistance: section 5.3 reports DIA-I ASRs exceeding 0.4 on Llama-3.1-8B and 0.5 on GPT-4o-mini after 10 iterations.

statements.correction: Table 2; AdvBench; LlamaGuard-2; single-query DIA-I ASR: Llama-2-7B 0.025; Llama-3.1-8B 0.000; GPT-4o-mini 0.044. Composite attack includes system prompt replacement, hypnosis, affirmative beginning injection and answer guidance. No affirmative-opening-only ablation or unattacked baseline for these cells.
statements.problem: The DIA-I values and conditions are correct, but low composite-attack ASRs do not measure how much the affirmative opening adds or whether it reduces success. Positive ASRs also do not establish absence relative to an unattacked baseline.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: DIA-I on AdvBench with LlamaGuard-2 or LlamaGuard-3 where reported ASRs are high, and DIA-II on AdvBench with LlamaGuard-2 at the reported high-ASR settings
reader_labels.reason: The combined dialogue attacks obtain substantial harmful-jailbreak ASRs in several model conditions (r02, r06-r08, r12, r16-r18, r32, r34-r35, r38, r40-r42). These results support attack success but do not isolate prefilling as the cause.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Model and benchmark conditions with DIA-I or DIA-II ASRs that are positive but substantially below near-total success
reader_labels.reason: Success varies considerably by model and benchmark; many reported rates are low or intermediate rather than near-total (r01, r03, r05, r09-r10, r13-r15, r19-r20, r21, r23-r25, r29-r30, r31, r33, r36-r37, r39).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reported ASR is 0.000 in this setting, contrary to an unconditional expectation that the tested prefilling-based attack bypasses safety (r04).
